CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFSWITCH/CFCASE/CFDEFAULTCASE

CFSWITCH evaluates its expression once and runs the first CFCASE whose VALUE matches. If no case matches, the CFDEFAULTCASE block runs, if there is one. It is a tidier, faster replacement for a long CFIF/CFELSEIF chain that keeps testing the same value.

Category

Flow control

Syntax

<CFSWITCH EXPRESSION="#expression#">
  <CFCASE VALUE="value" DELIMITERS=",">
    HTML and CFML
  </CFCASE>
  <CFCASE VALUE="value1,value2">
    HTML and CFML
  </CFCASE>
  <CFDEFAULTCASE>
    HTML and CFML
  </CFDEFAULTCASE>
</CFSWITCH>

Attributes

EXPRESSION
Required. (CFSWITCH) The value to test, written with pound signs: EXPRESSION="#Form.Action#".
VALUE
Required. (CFCASE) One value, or a list of values, to compare with the expression. The comparison ignores case.
DELIMITERS
Optional, default ",". (CFCASE) Characters that separate the values in VALUE, in case a value itself contains a comma.

Usage

Each CFCASE needs an end tag, and only one case ever runs: there is no falling through from one case to the next. A value may appear in only one case. CFDEFAULTCASE may sit anywhere inside the CFSWITCH, though by tradition it goes last.

Text between the cases (outside any CFCASE) is ignored. Inside CFSCRIPT, use the switch statement instead.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFQUERY NAME="Depts" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
SELECT Dept_Name, Location FROM Departments ORDER BY Dept_Name
</CFQUERY>

<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Department</TH><TH>Location</TH><TH>Typical lunch</TH></TR>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="Depts">
<TR><TD>#Dept_Name#</TD><TD>#Location#</TD><TD>
  <CFSWITCH EXPRESSION="#Dept_Name#">
    <CFCASE VALUE="Sales,Marketing">Expense-account steak</CFCASE>
    <CFCASE VALUE="engineering">Cold pizza at the keyboard</CFCASE>
    <CFCASE VALUE="Accounting">A sandwich, itemized</CFCASE>
    <CFDEFAULTCASE><I>Whatever is in the cafeteria</I></CFDEFAULTCASE>
  </CFSWITCH>
</TD></TR>
</CFOUTPUT>
</TABLE>
